title: kv-cache-attn-seqlen-edgecase-debug-scratchpad-15
content:
Context / high level:
- Intermittent correctness failures observed when sequence length crosses certain thresholds (~2048, 4096).
- Failures show up as corrupted continuation tokens in long chats from dedicated instances (NVIDIA H100, A100).
- Hypothesis: interaction between KV cache indexing + attention-kernel selection (optimized vs generic) leads to off-by-one reads for some seqlen combos.

What I observed (symptoms):
- Reproducer: batch of two requests, one short (len ~32) and one long (len ~2050). When the long request is served on same model shard, tokens after ~2048 appear scrambled.
- Happens only when runtime selects the 'optimized-kernel-v2' (fast fused attention). Falls back to 'generic-kernel' -> corruption disappears.
- Not consistently reproducible on local dev (small), more common under high concurrency or when batching enabled.

Logs / error snippets:
- Runtime attention selection log (info level):
  [2026-02-24 17:12:03.412] model=redwood/7b kernel=optimized-kernel-v2 reason=throughput_good seq_len=2050 batch=3
- Token mismatch diff (gold vs produced):
  gold: "..the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog"
  out : "..the quick brow0n f0x jumps �ver the lazy dog"
- GPU segfault stack trace (rare):
  #0  __device_stub__ZNK10Attention... (pc 0x7f3b...)
  #1  cudaLaunchKernel
  backtrace: (libcudart.so.11 + )
- Runtime check failure inserted in KV read: index >= kv_size -> printed once when reproducing with ASAN-like checks enabled.

Commands / reproducer runs tried:
- baseline run (single request, small):
  ./rwinf-runtime --model redwood/7b --batching=off --kernel=auto --input=repro_short.json
- failing run (batching on, mixed seqlen):
  ./rwinf-runtime --model redwood/7b --batching=on --batch_size=8 --kernel=auto --input=repro_mixed.json
- forced kernel runs:
  ./rwinf-runtime --model redwood/7b --kernel=optimized-kernel-v2 --input=repro_mixed.json   # failure reproduced
  ./rwinf-runtime --model redwood/7b --kernel=generic-kernel --input=repro_mixed.json        # passes
- ASAN-style debug build with extra bounds checks:
  BUILD_TYPE=debug make runtime && ./rwinf-runtime --checks=kv_bounds --kernel=optimized-kernel-v2 --input=repro_mixed.json
  -> prints: "KV read index 2048 >= kv_size 2048" once, then graceful fallback to generic-kernel in that run.
- GDB + cuda-memcheck (slow):
  cuda-memcheck ./rwinf-runtime --kernel=optimized-kernel-v2 --input=repro_mixed.json
  -> shows invalid global read in attention kernel when seq_len==2049 path taken.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Off-by-one in KV indexing when merging cache slices across micro-batches. Condition triggered when total kv_length == boundary (e.g., 2048) and next token forces allocation/stride change. Explains reproducibility at 2048/4096.
2) Kernel selection uses heuristics based on observed sequence distributions; a race where selection is evaluated before the batched KV lengths are updated, leading to kernel mismatch and stale assumptions about kv layout.
3) An alignment/stride assumption in optimized-kernel-v2 for block sizes of 32/64 that doesn't hold for odd seqlen (e.g., 2049) leading to miscalculated addresses.
4) Rare GPU memory allocator coalescing bug interacting with custom allocator (tcmalloc) in our runtime, causing reallocation thresholds at 2048*D size.

Evidence for (1) / why I think it's most likely:
- The debug run printed kv index >= kv_size precisely at boundary value 2048.
- Reproduces deterministically if we force batching with a batch that causes kv total to equal 2048 then append another request.
- Switching to generic kernel avoids the code path that relies on packed/contiguous KV layout assumptions.

Quick code pointers (where I looked):
- runtime/kv_cache/kv_cache_shard.cc: merge_kv_slices(), compute_global_kv_offset() -> suspect offsets arithmetic.
- runtime/kernels/attention/optimized_v2.cu: uses BLOCK_SIZE and assumes kv contiguous padding; check loads at line ~412.
- scheduler/batcher.cc: compute_batch_kv_length() -> should be in sync with kernel selection.

Small reproducer (python) I used locally:

python repro_mixed.py
# sequence: short prompt (32), long prompt (2050)
# sends as single batch via runtime GRPC test client with batching enabled

Observed locally: failure only when runtime.batching.max_batch_delay_ms > 0 and batch contains mixed lengths.

Temporary mitigation already deployed to 2 dev hosts:
- Force kernel selection -> generic-kernel for configs where max_seq_len >= 2048 (safe wall). Set flag: --kernel=generic-kernel-if-kv-boundary
- Also added a runtime assert to detect kv_index >= kv_size and fallback to generic kernel immediately (hotfix).

Next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Add unit tests for compute_global_kv_offset() covering boundary sizes (2047,2048,2049,4095,4096,4097). (Jared)
- [ ] Add instrumentation: emit KV-summary (kv_total_slots, kv_alloc_stride, kernel_selected) to logs at debug level when batch_size>1. (Maya)
- [ ] Reproduce on dedicated infra with H100 farm under load (set up A/B with kernel forced). (me)
- [ ] Code audit of optimized-kernel-v2 addressing math; add defensive min(kv_size, computed_index) clamps where safe. (me + Maya)
- [ ] If confirmed, prepare small rollback (default to generic-kernel) and perf comparison to quantify impact. (Ops + SRE)
- [ ] Link a proper failing unit test to RW-serve-PR#2197 and include repro json files. (Jared)

Open questions / things I couldn't rule out:
- Is there any step where compute_batch_kv_length() uses stale shard metadata because of lock-free updates? Need to verify batcher acquires proper snapshot of shard metadata.
- Could the optimized kernel be compiled with different padding assumptions per arch (H100 vs A100)? Check compile flags, especially any arch-specific constants in build scripts.
- Memory fragmentation still possible; need to run with forced malloc arenas disabled to rule out allocator behavior.

Notes from quick chat with Maya (02/26):
- Maya: "saw similar indexing bug months ago when adding prefix-caching optimization. Might be same root cause."
- Suggested: compare compute_global_kv_offset() output between debug and optimized paths for same input batch and print deltas.

Reproducer artifacts attached/available (local):
- repro_mixed.json (contains two requests payloads)
- repro_mixed.py (grpc client)
- debug build: /tmp/rwinf-runtime-debug

If anyone picks this up: start with adding bounds checks and unit tests for compute_global_kv_offset() and batching edgecases. That will likely surface the off-by-one quickly and is low-risk to land.

Scratchpad notes (short):
- observed boundaries: 512, 1024, 2048, 4096 (power-of-two-ish) -> alignment issue suspicion.
- adding +1 padding to kv allocation stopped repro in local runs (sanity check).
- gating optimized-kernel selection on "kv_total_slots % BLOCK_SIZE == 0" prevented failure in quick experiments.

-- Ethan
